persistentBatch.note: Same source with the persistent batch mode (task 11393): `serve --jobs LIST.json` initialises the plan, the prover and both program keys once, then runs chunk jobs, range merges and the Groth16 root in one process. Per-job artifacts keep the per-job names, formats and metric keys; a job whose proof.bin exists is SDK-verified and skipped. SP1 compressed proofs are randomised, so a proof is verified, never compared byte for byte.

twoGpuBatch.note: Task 11403: `serve --jobs LIST.json --gpus 0,1` runs one worker process per device for the independent jobs, then the dependent jobs in the coordinator. A job may pin a device with a `gpu` field; the rest are balanced by frame bytes. Each worker gets its own CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and a private TMPDIR. A failed worker stops the run before the dependent jobs and leaves the other artifacts on disk.
twoGpuBatch.buildCommand: cargo build --offline --locked --release -j 8 -p volume-chunk-host --bin volume-range-proof --bin volume-range-groth16 --features groth16-native

twoGpuBatch.measuredSpeedup: MEASURED chunk phase 422 s against 564.2 s of single-worker chunk proves = 1.34x, not the modelled 1.95x. Each chunk pays 18-33 % more while the other card proves: chunk-0 218.12 vs 164.53 s, chunk-3 154.31 vs 124.12 s, chunk-2 167.79 vs 142.28 s, chunk-1 161.67 vs 133.27 s. The two cards are independent, so host CPU and memory bandwidth are the limit. The byte balancer gave 372.4 s against 329.5 s of proves, a 13 % imbalance.

twoGpuBatch.cpuEquivalence: MEASURED on the CPU path: the two-worker coordinator splits two chunks across two workers and the merged per-job public values equal the single-worker batch. cargo test --test batch_two_gpu: 1 passed, finished in 1628.03 s, exit 0, 2026-09-16T22:28:21Z.
twoGpuBatch.containerFinding: The CUDA path needs one container per GPU: sp1-cuda 6.7.0 hardcodes the server socket as /tmp/sp1-cuda-<visible device index>.sock, so two workers in one container collide on /tmp/sp1-cuda-0.sock.
twoGpuBatch.measuredHostNote: CAUTION: every run on 2026-09-16 shared gpubox with the Nitro restore job and reviewer builds, so host load was 19-30 on 24 threads. Read the seconds above with that load. Two contention follow-ups ran under the same guard: CCD-disjoint cpusets (0-5,12-17 and 6-11,18-23) with --cpus 12 gave a 392 s chunk phase, the same cpusets with --cpus 4 gave 449 s, against 422 s unpinned at --cpus 4. The pinned shape is not adopted, because the 4-CPU pinned run is above the unpinned run. The plan input stays this measured table (34 chunks 3,178 s, grace 91,153 blocks).
